articles.title: Ministros do STF discutem se Moraes e Mendonça devem participar de julgamento na terça | G1
articles.standfirst: Quórum da sessão pode ser uma das questões preliminares a serem debatidas. Nos bastidores, ministros não descartam pedido de vista ou até adiamento da sessão para discutir caso de Moraes.
articles.summary: Quórum da sessão pode ser uma das questões preliminares a serem debatidas. Nos bastidores, ministros não descartam pedido de vista ou até adiamento da sessão para discutir caso de Moraes.
articles.body:
O Supremo Tribunal Federal chega às vésperas da sessão desta terça-feira (15) que pode decidir sobre a abertura de uma apuração contra o ministro Alexandre de Moraes por mensagens enviadas por Daniel Vorcaro sem definição do rito e principalmente do quórum que vai analisar o relatório da Polícia Federal.

Ministros discutem nos bastidores se os colegas Alexandre de Moraes e André Mendonça devem participar da sessão que vai decidir sobre a regularidade do relatório.

Até agora, o Supremo só confirmou que a sessão será transmitida na TV Justiça e o acesso ao plenário restrito.

Alvo do relatório da Polícia Federal que apontou 52 mensagens de Vorcaro , Moraes indicou em conversas internas que ainda não teria decidido se vai ou não pedir para se manifestar e até mesmo votar.

Uma ala do Supremo avalia que o ideal seria que Moraes não comparecesse ao plenário para não representar um movimento de pressão sobre os colegas.

Já ministros alinhados com Moraes também discutem se vão levantar uma questão de ordem para que o ministro André Mendonça não possa participar da análise do caso.

Os ministros Alexandre de Moraes e André Mendonça, do Supremo Tribunal Federal — Foto: REUTERS/Adriano Machado

O argumento é de que os questionamentos pela condução do relatório sobre Moraes impediria que votasse no caso.

A Procuradoria-Geral da República defendeu a nulidade do relatório e argumentou que Mendonça não só direcionou a busca de dados contra Moraes pela PF, como não consultou a Presidência sobre as medidas contra os colegas. Portanto, uma das possibilidades é que, se os ministros não decidirem o afastamento por iniciativa própria, o caso possa ser colocado para discussão do plenário.

Ao assumir a relatoria do caso de Moraes para a sessão, o presidente do STF , Edson Fachin, afirmou que, a depender do resultado da sessão, poderia ser aplicado trecho do Código de Processo Civil sobre o impedimento do relator.

Fachin conversou com Mendonça no sábado (12) sobre a medida, que foi elogiada por ministros alinhados a Moraes.

Fachin rejeita discutir na mesma sessão os casos dos ministros Moraes e Mendonça — Foto: Jornal Nacional/Reprodução

Outra possiblidade é que os ministros ainda discutam a participação de outros ministros que supostamente teriam algum tipo de citação no caso Master, como Dias Toffoli , Kassio Nunes Marques e Luiz Fux .

Toffoli deixou a relatoria do caso Master após a PF apontar relação do ministro e empresa da família com Vorcaro. Em relação a Nunes e Fux há uma possível menção a filhos dos ministros no material. Os três ministros negam qualquer irregularidade. A tendência é que o plenário apoie a participação de Fux e Nunes Marques.

O quórum da sessão pode ser uma das questões preliminares a ser debatida.

Nos bastidores, ministros não descartam um pedido de vista ou até mesmo o adiamento da sessão para discutir caso de Moraes. Outro ponto em aberto é se não haverá discussão sobre a sessão ser fechada.

articles.title: Como funciona a folga eleitoral e quais são seus direitos? | G1
articles.standfirst: Quem trabalha como mesário ou é convocado pela Justiça Eleitoral para outros serviços relacionados às eleições, tem direito a dois dias de compensação por cada dia trabalhado.
articles.summary: Quem trabalha como mesário ou é convocado pela Justiça Eleitoral para outros serviços relacionados às eleições, tem direito a dois dias de compensação por cada dia trabalhado.
articles.body:
Mesário conferindo documento / Eleição — Foto: Tomaz Silva/Agência Brasil

Quem trabalha nas eleições como mesário ou exerce outra função convocada pela Justiça Eleitoral tem direito à chamada "folga eleitoral" . O benefício garante dois dias de folga para cada dia de serviço prestado, sem desconto no salário ou prejuízo de outros direitos trabalhistas .

A regra vale apenas para quem tem vínculo empregatício, seja na iniciativa privada ou no serviço público. O benefício é garantido pela Lei das Eleições (Lei nº 9.504/1997).

Têm direito à folga os eleitores convocados pela Justiça Eleitoral para atuar nas eleições, como:

pessoas requisitadas para auxiliar os trabalhos eleitorais.

Quantos dias de folga o trabalhador recebe?

Para cada dia trabalhado nas eleições, o trabalhador tem direito a dois dias de folga. Na conta entram não apenas os dias de votação, mas também os treinamentos oficiais promovidos pela Justiça Eleitoral.

Por exemplo: se um mesário participar de um dia de treinamento. trabalhar no primeiro turno e trabalhar no segundo turno, terá direito a seis dias de folga (três dias de serviço multiplicados por dois) .

A folga vale para trabalhadores da iniciativa privada?

Sim. O direito vale para trabalhadores com carteira assinada (CLT) e também para servidores públicos , desde que tenham vínculo de trabalho no período em que foram convocados pela Justiça Eleitoral.

As folgas devem ser concedidas sem desconto no salário, nas férias ou em qualquer outra vantagem trabalhista .

Os dias de folga devem ser definidos em comum acordo entre o trabalhador e o empregador. As dispensas podem ser concedidas de uma só vez ou em datas diferentes, desde que seja respeitado o direito do trabalhador e considerada a organização da empresa ou do órgão público.

Para solicitar a folga, o trabalhador deve apresentar a declaração de participação fornecida pela Justiça Eleitoral. O documento informa os dias em que o eleitor prestou serviço e serve como comprovação para a concessão das folgas.

O direito à folga está vinculado ao emprego existente no momento da convocação para o serviço eleitoral. Caso haja mudança de emprego ou interrupção do vínculo de trabalho, a utilização das folgas deverá ser ajustada conforme a situação, para garantir o exercício do benefício.

Há outros benefícios para quem trabalha nas eleições?

Sim. Além das folgas compensatórias, quem atua como mesário ou auxiliar da Justiça Eleitoral também pode receber outros benefícios, que não são concedidos pela empresa empregadora, como:

auxílio-alimentação nos dias de votação;

vantagem como critério de desempate em concursos públicos, quando previsto no edital;

aproveitamento da atividade como horas complementares em instituições de ensino que adotem essa possibilidade.

articles.standfirst: Você pode consultar o seu local de votação pelo autoatendimento eleitoral, no portal do TSE, ou pelo aplicativo e-Título. Série de vídeos do g1 explica as eleições de 2026, os cargos em disputa e tira dúvidas.
articles.summary: Local de votação e horário das Eleições 2026 podem ser consultados pelo e-Título ou portal do TSE, garantindo que o eleitor vote no período unificado de Brasília.
articles.body:
Vai votar e não lembra onde é a sua seção? Está na dúvida sobre horário? É fácil descobrir. Você pode consultar o seu local de votação pelo autoatendimento eleitoral, no portal do TSE, ou pelo aplicativo e-título.

No autoatendimento , é só acessar a opção "onde votar" e informar os dados.

No e-título , o endereço da sua seção eleitoral aparece logo na tela inicial.

A série também aborda o impacto das novas tecnologias na campanha, como inteligência artificial, deepfakes e influenciadores.

Agora, sobre a hora, tem um detalhe importante: a votação começa às 8 da manhã e termina às 5 da tarde , pelo horário de Brasília. Isso significa que a votação começa e termina ao mesmo tempo em todo o país.

Mas, nos estados com fuso diferente de Brasília, o relógio local vai marcar outro horário. Por isso, é importante conferir qual é o horário da votação onde você mora.

articles.summary: President Trump on Sunday said $5,000 dividend checks will “happen 100 percent” if the GOP maintains its majority in Congress after the midterm elections. articles.body:
President Trump on Sunday said $5,000 dividend checks will “happen 100 percent” if the GOP maintains its majority in Congress after the midterm elections.

The president compared the potential payouts to the $1,776 checks that went out to U.S. service members, telling reporters outside Air Force One on Sunday that he’s received the same type of pushback.

“The $5,000 is going to happen 100 percent,” he said. “And the reason is because our country is taking in trillions and trillions of dollars. And it’s going to happen.”

Trump said he will not send the dividends out while the GOP has control of Congress.

“I don’t want to do it now, because if the Democrats get it, our country will be in shambles and they won’t be able to do it,” he continued. “If we get in, we’re taking in tremendous amounts of money. We’re taking in over $20 trillion in terms of investment. And with the Democrats, all of that money will be thrown out. If the Democrats get in, they won’t be able to pay it.”

The president first pledged the checks last Wednesday during the Republican National Committee’s (RNC) midterm convention. He said his administration can disburse the proposed dividends “because we’ve done so well,” adding that the payments will only be used in the U.S.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said Thursday that the dividends would not rely on taxpayer dollars , but that the administration could “earn the money that Donald Trump wants to pay out, not from the deficit and not from taxpayers.”

White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett suggested that they could materialize via a reconciliation package through Congress, which holds appropriating power. The administration cannot spend public money on anything without funds set aside by lawmakers.

The $1,776 checks sent to around 1.45 million service members last year were part of a one-time housing supplement added to Trump’s sweeping tax and spending law known as the One Big Beautiful Bill.

Rep. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) quickly announced after Trump’s pledge that he would introduce a bill in Congress to ensure these checks happen.

Paul Berman, a professor at George Washington University Law School, previously told The Hill that tariff revenue would not cover the estimated $1.3 trillion it would take to dole out the checks. The president’s tariffs have generated roughly $341 billion in net revenue since the start of 2025, according to Treasury Department data cited by the Bipartisan Policy Center.

“Even if there were, that’s money that goes back to the public fisc, and then Congress is the one that has the power of the purse to allocate it,” Berman said.

But the Supreme Court struck down the Trump administration’s sweeping tariffs, ordering a refund of $166 billion of what was generated.

Some Republicans disagree with the dividends. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) highlighted the national debt and suggested that it would lead to more inflation.

“From the few details we have, it seems that the proposed $5,000 dividend would not have an income cap and would be extraordinarily costly,” Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) said about the dividends.

articles.title: Texas Republicans call out railroad commissioner candidate over racist social media post
articles.summary: Several prominent Texas Republicans on Sunday condemned a racist post by Bo French, a GOP candidate for statewide office to regulate Texas’ oil and gas industry.
articles.body: Several prominent Texas Republicans on Sunday condemned a racist post by Bo French, a GOP candidate for statewide office to regulate Texas’ oil and gas industry. French, who is running for state railroad commissioner, posted a photo of students of South Asian descent at the University of Texas celebrating the school’s football win over Ohio State on Saturday, saying, “The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined.” French was quickly met with backlash from his own party, as Sen. John Cornyn, who is leaving Congress after he lost in a primary to Trump-backed state Attorney General Ken Paxton, condemned the post and urged fellow Republicans to do the same. “This is the Republican nominee for statewide office. Are other Republican elected officials going to condemn the intolerance and racism, or look the other way while it becomes normalized. This is how great political parties self-destruct. Sad,” Cornyn wrote on X. French responded by calling Cornyn a “RINO” and saying Texas institutions were “overrun by illegal aliens and foreign nationals.” “He and the other America Last losers are mad that Texas Republicans are starting to put America First,” French wrote. Rep. Dan Crenshaw, R-Texas, condemned French on X as well, while Democratic state Rep. Jon Rosenthal, who is running against French for railroad commissioner, said French could not “tell a Longhorn from a foreigner.” Gov. Greg Abbott did not condemn the post in a statement Sunday, but he said that French’s message was not his and that the photo he posted was “selective” and “shows a way that Texans unite.” “The way we win the state is the same way we win football games. We unite under the brand of Texas,” Abbott said. “That doesn’t mean that Texas cannot also lead in having the toughest immigration laws of any state in America and freezing H-1B visas at our universities.” French in May defeated the Abbott-endorsed incumbent, Jim Wright, for the GOP nomination for railroad commissioner. Texas House Speaker Dustin Burrows called on French to delete the post, writing: “You can oppose immigration policy without demeaning people because of their race or ethnicity — this post has crossed the line.” The Democratic nominee for the Senate, James Talarico, lauded Cornyn for his statement, while condemning French’s post and questioning his opponent, Paxton, about whether he, too, would speak out against it. “Racism has no place in Texas,” Talarico wrote. Paxton responded to Talarico’s post by saying he condemned “racism in all its forms” — without making mention of French or French’s post and while attacking Talarico. French has a history of making bigoted remarks. He has used slurs against the LGBTQ community and has made antisemitic and Islamophobic remarks. French did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Asked by WFAA-TV of Dallas in July whether he regretted those comments, French said he did not, adding, “Truth sounds like hate to those who hate the truth.” The Texas Railroad Commission is a powerful three-member panel that regulates oil and gas production, pipelines and natural gas utilities in the state. Members serve six-year terms. A spokesperson for the University of Texas did not immediately respond to a request for comment Sunday about French’s post.

articles.title: Kennedy Center could close as early as Tuesday, warns of bankruptcy, documents show
articles.summary: Leaders of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, installed by President Donald Trump, say the center is on the brink of bankruptcy and argue th...
articles.body:
Kennedy Center could close as early as Tuesday, warns of bankruptcy, documents show

Leaders of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, installed by President Donald Trump, say the center is on the brink of bankruptcy and argue that putting the president's name on its facade - and thus ensuring his fundraising efforts - may be the only way to avoid imminent and "certain fiscal collapse," according to documents obtained by The Washington Post.

The bleak assessment is laid out in a 57-page packet distributed to the center's board of trustees ahead of a special meeting Tuesday, when the Trump-led board is scheduled to consider two resolutions aimed at addressing twin crises confronting the national performing arts center: one financial, the other physical. Center officials say they could be unable to make payroll or pay routine maintenance contracts "within a matter of weeks" and argue that publicly recognizing Trump could secure his help raising enough money to keep the institution afloat.

Center officials are also recommending that the board close its main building immediately, warning that remaining open would endanger lives. Board approval, which seems likely, means the center could close as early as Tuesday.

The presentation makes clear that Trump's support hinges on getting public credit for his involvement. The financial resolution says Trump has offered to "raise the necessary funds to keep the Center from bankruptcy" while the building undergoes a sweeping renovation. But it says Trump is unlikely to provide "fundamental oversight" of that project or lead a financial rescue without "appropriate recognition" of his role.

Together, the two proposals represent a remarkable new phase in Trump's takeover of the Kennedy Center, which has been engulfed by financial turmoil, leadership upheaval and litigation since he installed himself as chairman last year. Trump and his allies have repeatedly portrayed his leadership - and his name - as essential to rescuing the institution, even as ticket sales and fundraising have plummeted under their stewardship.

Trustees are being asked to choose among 10 texts that could be placed on the building's exterior beneath its name, including one reading: "Renovation Restoration and Endowment overseen by President Donald J. Trump and the Trump Kennedy Center Fund."

Lawyers for Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-Ohio), a Kennedy Center trustee who has sued to keep Trump's name off the building, blasted the new proposal.

"This constant effort to add Donald Trump's name to the Kennedy Center facade is the definition of insanity," lawyers Norm Eisen and Nathaniel Zelinsky said in a statement. "This is now the third attempt to deface this sacred memorial and turn it into a vanity project for one man's ego.

"Worse still, now Trump is taking the Center hostage and threatening to in effect kill it unless he gets his way," they added. "This has to stop."

The proposal comes less than a month after the board approved a similar plan to inscribe "Restored and Renovated by President Donald J. Trump" on the facade. U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper, who ruled in May that only Congress can rename the Kennedy Center and ordered Trump's name removed, is considering a legal challenge to that proposal.

The center's stark new financial assessment is also a dramatic departure from the turnaround its leaders touted publicly for much of Trump's tenure.

Internal budgets and forecasts obtained by The Washington Post earlier this year showed ticket sales and fundraising plunging after the board added Trump's name to the building in December. By May, officials projected the center would collect about $124 million of the $220 million in revenue it had budgeted for the fiscal year, leaving a roughly $23 million deficit even after substantial spending cuts. A center spokesperson blamed the problems on financial mismanagement by previous leadership and said Trump's name had attracted new donors.

The second resolution before trustees Tuesday would address what management describes as an increasingly urgent threat from the deteriorating building itself.

Executive Director Matt Floca, who was installed by Trump in March, told trustees that during a severe storm Sept. 4, a roughly four-by-five-foot section of ceiling plaster broke loose in the Grand Foyer and fell about 60 feet, scattering debris near the Concert Hall entrance. No one was injured. Inspectors found at least seven other locations with visible water-related deterioration, according to the board packet.

Separately, engineers examining the outside of the building found widespread corrosion in structural components of the soffit panels that form the underside of an overhang wrapping around the center, Floca said in a two-page memo to trustees. Of roughly half of the building's 278 panels examined, 46 had severe structural corrosion and another 93 had mild-to-moderate corrosion, he said, adding that engineers projected that about one-third require immediate replacement. The report says 2,500-pound ceiling assemblies hang roughly 60 feet above public walkways.

A draft resolution says Floca and Delta Consulting Group, which has reviewed the center's renovation plans, determined that the building is "unsafe for continued occupancy" and that delaying renovations would pose further danger to employees and the public.

Kennedy Center representatives declined to comment on the proposals, but sent a previous statement from spokeswoman Roma Daravi, "Another example of the urgent need to close for renovation and revitalization, as our Chairman President Trump has championed. Fortunately, no one was injured when the main hall's ceiling collapsed. This structural failure stems from decades of neglect and deferred maintenance by the previous leadership, and there's no justification for further delays in restoring America's cultural center."

Trump first proposed closing the Kennedy Center for two years in February, saying an empty building would allow crews to renovate it more quickly. His board approved the plan in March, but Cooper blocked the closure in May, finding trustees had relied on insufficient information and had not adequately weighed the consequences. He allowed the board to reconsider after a more thorough review.

Trustees did so Aug. 13, again approving a two-year shutdown as part of a roughly $250 million renovation.

Tuesday's resolution would go considerably further by ordering the main building closed immediately. Management says repairs cannot safely be performed around audiences and employees because structural work, electrical shutdowns and construction would affect interconnected systems and public areas throughout the building.

The Reach, the center's newer expansion, would remain open, while performances and other programming would continue at other venues.

articles.title: Trump says China 'spies' on US after report ties Chinese imagery to Iran strike
articles.summary: The president said the U.S. spies on China "too" after a report linked Chinese satellite imagery to Iran's deadly July missile attack on American troops.
articles.body: President Donald Trump said Sunday that China "spies on us" just as "we spy on them," following a report that Chinese entities provided Iran with satellite imagery before a deadly missile attack that killed three U.S. troops. While speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One, Trump was asked about a Wall Street Journal report that Chinese entities allegedly supplied Iran with high-resolution satellite imagery of Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan before Tehran's July 17 missile attack. "They basically do what we do," Trump said. TRUMP GIVES SMITHSONIAN DAYS TO REPLACE 'STRANGE MODERNIST SCULPTURE' WITH FOUNDING FATHER Asked whether he planned to raise the issue with Chinese President Xi Jinping when he visits the U.S., Trump said Xi has "behaved reasonably well," and that "we behave reasonably well." "You know what they say? That China spies on us. I say you're right, and we spy on them, too," Trump said. TRUMP TELLS ZELENSKYY TO STOP DOING 'ONE THING' DURING ATTACKS ON RUSSIA According to The Wall Street Journal, U.S. officials linked the imagery to Iran's July 17 strike on the Jordanian base, which killed three U.S. troops. Officials described it as the clearest evidence to date that support from Chinese entities for Iran during the war has had deadly consequences for American forces, the outlet reported. TRUMP SAYS HE WOULD 'LOVE' TO SEE IRELAND UNIFIED AS ONE NATION The U.S. officials did not identify the Chinese entities involved or accuse Beijing of direct involvement in the attack. articles.title: Trump says Ukraine should halt Russian refinery strikes amid surging diesel prices
articles.summary: President Trump on Sunday said Ukraine should hold off on its strikes on Russian oil refineries, citing the growing surge in diesel prices amid the Iran war and subsequent energy crisis. A reporter asked Trump while at his golf course in Ireland, during the Irish Open, whether he had talked to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky…
articles.body:
President Trump on Sunday said Ukraine should hold off on its strikes on Russian oil refineries, citing the growing surge in diesel prices amid the Iran war and subsequent energy crisis.

A reporter asked Trump while at his golf course in Ireland, during the Irish Open, whether he had talked to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky since speaking with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump then called on Zelensky to stop the strikes.

“Mr. Zelenskyy has to do one thing,” Trump said. “He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia. We spoke to Mr. Zelenskyy about it. There are plenty of other targets. Don’t hit diesel fuel, because that’s hurting, that’s hurting the world.”

The president said that diesel prices were going up because “it’s having a hard time coming out of Russia.”

“And if that’s the case, that hurts the world,” Trump continued. “We’ve got to stop it.”

The average cost of diesel broke records on Friday as it reached $6.05, a 63-percent increase from last year when a gallon of diesel was $3.71, according to AAA . These rising prices are expected to push up the cost of everyday goods.

Ukraine launched attacks on a refinery in Siberia on Thursday, creating fuel shortages in Russia, prompting Russia to retaliate on urban gas stations. One attack focused on the city of Nizhnekamsk, which is the home of several key oil refineries, while another drone attack hit a crucial refinery in Slavyansk-on-Kuban in Russia’s Krasnodar region near Crimea.

Russian forces have escalated the campaign against Ukraine with ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones striking Ukraine’s power grid ahead of the harsh winter season.

Gas prices have also skyrocketed in the more than six months after the U.S.-Israeli conflict in Iran began. Iran limited passage through the Strait of Hormuz, where roughly 20 percent of the world’s oil supply is exported, affecting gas prices but also risking fuel shortages for airlines and airports across the globe.

The U.S. and Iran have been in a stalemate over the strait, though both sides have carried out attacks on vessels and bases in the region. The regime’s state media reported on Sunday that an Iranian ship was struck by an “unidentified projectile,” quoting Hossein Amir Teymoori, the governor of Qeshm.

Trump has said the conflict will end after the midterm elections and suggested that gas prices “ will drop precipitously ” thereafter. He floated the idea on Sunday that the U.S. could go into Iran and “keep the oil, like Venezuela,” referring to the U.S. oil deal with the South American country months after U.S. forces captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.
